tagline: A blind, furry crab wearing a coat of bacteria
summary: Discovered in 2005 on hydrothermal vents in the South Pacific, the yeti crab is a pale squat lobster whose long arms are thickly furred with bristles. Those bristles host dense mats of bacteria that can draw energy from vent chemicals rather than sunlight.

stats.size: The described type specimen is 8.8 cm long; popular accounts give about 15 cm
stats.range: Hydrothermal vents on the Pacific–Antarctic Ridge, south of Easter Island
stats.diet: Probably omnivorous; may feed on bacteria grown on its bristles

facts.title: A 21st-century discovery
facts.text: The species was found in 2005 on the Pacific–Antarctic Ridge, about 1,500 km south of Easter Island, at roughly 2,200 m depth, living around hydrothermal vents.

facts.title: So new it needed a family
facts.text: It was so distinct from known crustaceans that scientists created a brand-new family, Kiwaidae, to hold it.

facts.title: A coat of microbes
facts.text: Its 'fur' is setae (stiff bristles) covered in dense filamentous bacteria. Their enzymes suggest they can fix carbon and process sulfur from vent fluids — chemosynthesis, making food from chemicals instead of light.

facts.title: Farmer or scavenger?
facts.text: Scientists suspect it eats the bacteria it grows, but this has not been directly observed in Kiwa hirsuta; its describers also saw it feeding on damaged mussel tissue.

facts.title: Nearly eyeless
facts.text: Yeti crabs' eyes are reduced to small, soft, unpigmented tissue — little use in the pitch-dark deep sea, and the animal is thought to be blind.

references.title: Dancing for Food in the Deep Sea: Bacterial Farming by a New Species of Yeti Crab (Thurber, Jones & Schnabel 2011)
Epibiotic bacteria associated with the recently discovered Yeti crab, Kiwa hirsuta (Goffredi et al. 2008, Environmental Microbiology)

image.alt: A pale, cream-coloured yeti crab seen from above against a black background, its two long arms covered in dense silky bristles ending in small claws
image.caption: A yeti crab collected from a hydrothermal vent on the Pacific–Antarctic Ridge at about 2,300 m
image.creator: Alexis Fifis (Ifremer)
